lectionaryreading.title: St. Paul's Letter to the Galatians 6:11-18

translation.title: Reading
translation.body: These Martyrs contested for the Faith during the reign of Diocletian, in the year 288. Saint Callistratus was arrested as a Christian, and after being tormented, was enclosed in a sack and cast into the sea. The sack burst, and the Saint came to dry land safe and sound. Forty-nine soldiers, seeing this, also confessed Christ, and with him were cast into prison, then beheaded.

hymn.title: Apolytikion of Martyr Callistratus & his Companions in the Fourth Tone
hymn.shorttitle: Apolytikion of Martyr Callistratus & his Companions

translation.body: Thy Martyrs, O Lord, in their courageous contest for Thee received as the prize the crowns of incorruption and life from Thee, our immortal God. For since they possessed Thy strength, they cast down the tyrants and wholly destroyed the demons' strengthless presumption. O Christ God, by their prayers, save our souls, since Thou art merciful.

hymn.title: Kontakion of Martyr Callistratus & his Companions in the Second Tone
hymn.shorttitle: Kontakion of Martyr Callistratus & his Companions

translation.body: O all-wise and godly Saints, today the whole Church, showing honour to you all, doth now in spirit sing your praise; for ye contested in her behalf, O right-victorious Martyrs of Christ our God.
